findings.statement:
The new statement-start mutating-keyword scan runs on sqlparse output that does not strip a MySQL '#' comment unless a space follows '#', so a prefix like '#x
' hides the leading verb: '#x
DO GET_LOCK(...)', '#c
SHUTDOWN' and '#c
START REPLICA' are all allowed in read-only mode. The CWE-184 bypass the PR set out to close is still open.

Blocking DO GET_LOCK while SELECT GET_LOCK, RELEASE_LOCK, replication-wait functions and sys_exec/sys_eval still pass makes the guard asymmetric: the read-shaped twin of the targeted threat bypasses it.

The statement-start test matrix varies only the keyword, never comment/whitespace obfuscation for a fixed keyword, so it cannot catch the '#'-comment bypass; add '#', '#x', '# ' and '#'-after-';' cases.
USE <db>, CACHE INDEX and LOAD INDEX INTO CACHE are statement-leading state changers that still pass the read-only gate (SET is blocked, USE is not).
All new tests call detect_mutating_keywords directly; none proves run_query rejects a new keyword end-to-end on the read-only path, where the security guarantee actually lives.

A ';' inside a string literal trips the anchored statement-start scan (e.g. WHERE note = 'do it; commit later' reports COMMIT), so the no-false-positive guarantee silently depends on the stacked-queries rule and the logged rejection reason is wrong.
